papers.title: Two-Stage Rotation-Based Joint ToA-AoA Estimation for Spatial Wideband Systems
papers.abstract: Joint delay-angle (time-of-arrival (ToA) and angle-of-arrival (AoA)) estimation in wideband multi-antenna orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems is a key enabler for localization, sensing, and extremely large-multiple input multiple output (XL-MIMO) communications in mmWave/THz bands. In this regime, the spatial wideband effect (SWE), also known as range-angle coupling in MIMO frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar, breaks the conventional spatial narrowband assumption; the energy of each path is spread over multiple delay-angle bins, and the dominant peak of the 2D-DFT spectrum no longer coincides with the true coarse grid location. As a result, standard DFT-based coarse estimation followed by rotation/maximum-likelihood fine-tuning becomes inherently biased. In this paper, we first develop a rigorous finite-dimensional characterization of this phenomenon. Using a 2D Dirichlet-kernel model, we derive closed-form bounds on the SWE-induced spreading width and show that the significant energy of a single path is confined to at most $\lceil αM |\tildeφ_i| \rceil$ bins in both angle and delay, where $α$ denotes the fractional bandwidth, $M$ the array size, and $\tildeφ_i$ the normalized AoA of the $ i$-th scatterer. Building on this analysis, we propose a two-stage per-path rotation framework. In the first stage, we apply a cluster-level removal of the wideband coupling term and perform a localized 2D search to correct the SWE-induced coarse-bin shift. In the second stage, we show that the residual wideband term is uniformly bounded and can be treated as a small perturbation; this justifies a narrowband-type rotation refinement that yields super-resolution off-grid estimates of AoA, ToA, and path gains with near-DFT complexity.

papers.title: Ego-OSCAR: Egocentric Open source Stereo CAptuRe System
papers.abstract: Egocentric vision has scaled its corpora far faster than its instruments. Calibrated stereo rigidly coupled to a synchronized inertial stream is not new; research-grade headsets deliver it. What does not exist is an open version: those platforms are closed products a third party cannot build or extend, and the consumer cameras used elsewhere are monocular and rolling-shutter. The instrument is the least reproducible part of an otherwise open pipeline. We present our system, an open-hardware head-mounted capture platform, at a complete bill of materials under USD 200 in commodity parts and 3D prints. It pairs a hardware-synchronized global-shutter stereo camera with a 6-axis IMU, an embedded Linux SBC for on-device encoding, and a real-time microcontroller that bridges the camera and inertial clock domains to a residual of 700 microseconds and watchdogs the recording against silent failure. We release the full stack alongside the device: CAD, firmware, recording and time-synchronization tooling, and our corpus, roughly 550 hours of stereo video over 1,462 sessions and 25 contributors, every device shipping its own stereo calibration. The corpus ships with model-predicted annotation layers rather than raw video alone, including per-frame 3D hand reconstructions spanning essentially the whole timeline; these are automatic predictions, not human-verified ground truth, and we report them as such. We characterize the instrument along sensor fidelity, data utility, and six months of distributed field deployment. Our system is not the highest fidelity egocentric rig; it is the cheapest one a reader of this paper can reproduce, and the only corpus here that others can extend rather than only consume.

papers.title: A Two-Stage Shape- and Motion-Aware Framework for mmWave-based Human Mesh Recovery
papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar has emerged as a promising sensing modality for human perception, offering robustness under challenging environmental conditions and strong privacy preservation. However, recovering accurate 3D human meshes from radar is difficult for two reasons: radar tensors contain significant environmental clutter, and each frame observes only part of the body surface. These challenges demand opposite operations, removing measured energy that does not belong to the body versus inferring geometry the sensor never measured. Yet previous works typically entangle both within a single network, with the mesh objective as the main supervision. We instead reformulate radar-based mesh recovery as two explicitly supervised sub-problems. A signal-level separation stage isolates body-related voxels through coarse-to-fine localization and voxel-wise segmentation, trained with visibility derived voxel labels. A structure-level reconstruction stage then recovers the body from this partial observation using a dual-branch network that jointly models per-frame shape and inter-frame motion. Experiments show that our method reduces mesh error by up to 9.1% over the strongest baseline while using over 10 $\times$ fewer parameters. Source code can be found via https://github.com/haipham03/mmTSM-Mesh

papers.title: Task-Oriented Semantic Communication for Hazard Warning and Remote Operation in Connected Vehicle Platoons
papers.abstract: Connected and automated vehicle platoons require reliable dissemination of task-relevant hazard information to enable appropriate downstream responses, with unresolved situations additionally requiring remote human intervention. However, the limited channel bandwidth of V2X communication makes high-volume sensor data transmission challenging, motivating the exchange of only task-relevant information rather than raw sensor data. The framework combines onboard instance segmentation and monocular depth estimation for task-oriented hazard decision-making with Stable Diffusion Variational Autoencoder (SD-VAE)-based semantic scene compression. Task-relevant hazard information and the compact semantic representation are jointly disseminated through a broadcast-based Emergency Semantic Message (ESM) over the existing V2X protocol stack. Evaluation demonstrates that SD-VAE consistently outperforms JPEG and JPEG 2000 on task-relevant reconstruction metrics, exhibiting graceful degradation rather than a sharp cliff effect under low-SINR conditions, demonstrating its feasibility for remote scene reconstruction when human intervention is required. Moreover, an extensive campaign of 7,290 simulation runs shows a low overall inter-vehicle collision rate of 0.99%, with collisions occurring mainly under extreme high-speed and short-gap conditions.

papers.title: TALON: Token-Aligned Lightweight Adapters for 6-DoF Spacecraft Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Monocular 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation methods predominantly process individual frames, discarding the temporal information present in an image sequence acquired during spacecraft manoeuvres. Few temporal approaches require full backbone fine-tuning or auxiliary optical flow networks, risking catastrophic forgetting or increasing computational cost, respectively. Pre-attention placement allows the frozen attention to reason over temporally enriched tokens, achieving stronger performance with a single adapter per block than post-attention alternatives. The alignment loss shapes the intermediate representations so that each keypoint induces a spatially precise activation in the token field, while the framework adds less than 5% parameters to the frozen backbone. On SPADES dataset, TALON reduces the pose error by 50% over the prior state-of-the-art, and on SwissCube dataset it surpasses the prior best by 21.8% in ADD-0.1d accuracy. Zero-shot cross-domain evaluation from sim-to-real on SPARK real data reduces pose error by 4.7x, and ablations characterise the role of adapter depth across in-domain and cross-domain settings.

papers.title: Active MIMO Sensing: Optimality Conditions and Exploration-Exploitation Tradeoff
papers.abstract: This paper develops an active sensing framework for designing the transmit and receive beamformers of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar system with a limited number of radio-frequency (RF) chains. In the proposed framework, the transmit and receive beamformers are adaptively designed in each sensing stage based on the measurements made in the previous sensing stages, and the optimization of the beamformers are based on the minimization of the Bayesian Cram{é}r-Rao bound (BCRB) for estimating the unknown sensing parameters. To address the exploration-exploitation tradeoff inherent in such an adaptive procedure, this paper proposes a two-phase design involving two variants of the BCRB optimization problem: an exploration-centric variant that requires multiple orthogonal beamforming directions to be probed in each sensing stage, followed by an exploitation-centric variant that optimizes the per-stage BCRB without such requirement. For both variants, the transmit and receive beamformers are optimized as two subproblems in an alternating fashion in each sensing stage. The alternating optimization is shown to converge to a stationary point of the per-stage BCRB optimization provided that each subproblem is solved to global optimality. A main contribution of this paper is to determine sufficient conditions under which global optimality can be guaranteed---despite that the two subproblems are nonconvex (due to the limited number of RF chains), by studying the structures of their optimal solutions via Lagrangian dual analysis. The conditions pertain to the multiplicity of the eigenvalues of specific direction matrices that can be analytically written in terms of the optimal dual variables. Simulation results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed design framework as compared to state-of-the-art adaptive beamforming strategies.

papers.title: DGT-Map: Directional Global Traversability Mapping Utilizing Multi-Task Learning for Heterogeneous Vehicles
papers.abstract: Off-road traversability is direction-dependent and vehicle specific, yet most global maps assign a single isotropic cost to each location. Existing learned estimators are also commonly trained independently for each vehicle; this preserves vehicle-specific behavior but prevents vehicles from sharing common terrain representations. DGT-MAP addresses both limitations through a self-supervised framework that learns global, directional, and vehicle-conditioned traversability costmaps from RGB-D observations and locomotion signals. A shared multi-task backbone learns common terrain features across training vehicles while vehicle-specific prediction heads preserve platform-dependent responses. At inference, DGT-MAP produces a heading-indexed costmap that can be used by a direction-aware planner. We evaluate DGT-MAP in simulation by integrating it into a Hybrid A* navigation stack and measuring downstream task success on challenging terrains, including slopes that are traversable downhill but not uphill and a ridge obstacle that is traversable by some vehicles, but not by others. Across evaluated tasks, DGT-MAP achieves the highest or tied-highest navigation success rate when compared against geometric, binary, and learned direction-agnostic baselines.

papers.title: IGLOSS: Image Generation for Lidar Open-vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
papers.abstract: This paper presents a new method for the zero-shot open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) of 3D automotive lidar data. To circumvent the recognized image-text modality gap that is intrinsic to approaches based on Vision Language Models (VLMs) such as CLIP, our method relies instead on image generation from text, to create prototype images. Given a 3D network distilled from a 2D Vision Foundation Model (VFM), we then label a point cloud by matching 3D point features with 2D image features of these prototypes. Our method is state-of-the-art for OVSS on nuScenes and SemanticKITTI. Code, pre-trained models and generated images are available at https://github.com/valeoai/IGLOSS.

papers.title: Integrated Sensing and Communication in 3GPP: Evolution from 5G-Advanced to 6G
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) extends mobile networks from information transfer toward perception of passive objects and environments. By exploiting propagation delay, Doppler, angle, and temporal variation, a mobile network can support detection and tracking while reusing licensed spectrum, infrastructure, and edge computing at network scale and under operator control. Unlike conventional radar, ISAC must additionally address multi-application access, heterogeneous sensing entities, uncertainty, privacy, trust, and integration with communication services. This article reviews the evolution of ISAC in 3GPP from 5G-Advanced to 6G. It explains Release-19 ISAC service requirements and channel models, the Release-20 sensing function architecture and reporting abstractions, and the 5G monostatic baseline for drone detection and tracking. It also examines 6G-native sensing, including passive object sensing, communication assistance, multiple sensing modes, and multi-source data integration. The article makes the evolution explicit through a comparison of sensing capabilities and KPIs, an assessment of reusable functions and deployment costs, and a quantitative UAV case study linking service targets to sensing configuration, reporting overhead, and delivery latency.

papers.title: FlatVPR: Plug-and-play Geo-linear Residual Adapter for Geometric Rectification of Foundation Model Feature Manifolds
papers.abstract: This paper proposes ``FlatVPR,'' a novel geometric rectification paradigm that effectively bridges the trade-off between map lightweightness and localization accuracy in visual place recognition (VPR) by enforcing a feature manifold structure where any descriptor between two adjacent anchors $\mathbf{z}_A$ and $\mathbf{z}_B$ can be accurately reconstructed via linear interpolation $\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{pseudo} = (1-t)\mathbf{z}_A + t\mathbf{z}_B$, where $t \in [0,1]$ denotes the relative position. While state-of-the-art foundation models such as DINOv2-ViT-S/14 provide robust semantic features, their latent manifolds exhibit prominent curvature, projecting uniform linear motion in physical space onto highly non-linear trajectories in the feature space, which hinders reliable reconstruction under sparse anchor conditions. To enable the aforementioned interpolation-based reconstruction, we introduce a residual transformation $\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \mathbf{z} + \text{Res}(\mathbf{z})$ to the raw foundation features $\mathbf{z}$, where $\text{Res}(\cdot)$ represents a learnable adapter. Our method explicitly suppresses manifold curvature using a mathematically grounded Pullback Flatness Loss that minimizes the deviation of intermediate features from the linear segment connecting adjacent anchors, thereby minimizing the intrinsic curvature of the manifold. Through this spatial flattening, map construction is formulated within an Expectation-Maximization (EM) framework, decoupled into a continuous M-step for manifold adaptation and a conceptual E-step for optimal anchor selection guidelines. Experiments on the NCLT dataset demonstrate that the application of our adapter leads to significant performance improvements even under extremely sparse anchor conditions with 100m intervals and extreme seasonal changes.
